item.content:encoded: This had me fully in tears, and I think the skillful buildup of that emotion made the sudden change of gears at the end feel like a blindside, increasing its impact exponentially. This reads as such a reflective, heartfelt piece that I forgot where I was a little bit, setting me up to be caught off-guard by the horror and really feel that too.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I didn't really get anything out of this. It felt more or less meandering in large part in the earlier sections, almost wallowing in the melancholy that you try and build up through her death. I think that could work just as a reflective piece but, suddenly marker-meat. My primary issue is that there's virtually no buildup to the spookies as they occur - the red Sharpie's something of a red flag early on but it's not really presented as such, so when marker-meat happens it feels pretty left field. I don't have much of an issue with the writing but the way it's structured and the ending really just stick out like two broken thumbs.

-1, I think I might like it a little more if this wasn't intended to be a spooky, but then again I wasn't so much of a fan of the earlier sections, so - maybe it just comes down to personal preference.

item.title: Re: +1
item.content:encoded:
Will correct!

Thank you for the feedback, I wasn't sure how well it would be received here, but I equally feel it fits into the Foundation-verse in some way I can't quite pinpoint. I'm glad you enjoyed it!

Very minor grammatical issue.

…Right?

Should be, to my knowledge…

… right?

Other than that, this is absolutely stellar. The use of the red sharpie made for a super chilling ending, and you spared no detail in making the last few lines impactful- you've distilled the well-trodden ground of 'back from the grave' to its very purest form very successfully. I'm really impressed by this.

item.title: Author's Note
item.content:encoded:
At last, a story not about Kit!

But it's kinda depressing, and it's kinda more a ghost story that hovers on the edge of the Foundationverse, so I don't know how it's going to go down.

Geez, I've been writing a lot of stories about suicide recently. Let's all blame it on the time of the year.

I didn't get this vetted on-site, so I'm doubtful about its success even as a creepypasta-Foundation Tale, but it's worth a shot.

As a note, yesterday was National Survivors of Suicide Day in the States. So. There's that.
